verses.mystical_translation: The divine hides in the deep veil; presence is mystery before human dwelling.
A house is made as an address for what cannot be confined.
A leader turns, blesses — the people rise to witness covenant speech.
Blessing names the faithfulness that makes speech become handiwork.
Divine choice precedes cities and rulers; presence decides place and office.
A place and a line are set so that memory and leadership bear the name.
A king's longing to build is a heart's offering toward name and place.
Divine commendation honors the heart's fidelity, even when action is delayed.
Promise passes through lineage: the task belongs to the next generation.
Speech becomes history; one takes the place of a father to fulfill the spoken word.
The ark holds the compact; the house receives that which binds the people.
A posture of intercession: open hands before altar and people.
An elevated place frames speech: measurement shapes liturgy.
The proclamation names uniqueness: covenant‑faithfulness and steadfast mercy as the divine signature.
Promise spoken, promise enacted — history bears the hand that fulfilled speech.
A plea to secure dynastic fidelity tied to covenantal obedience.
Request that divine speech find its seal in time and rule.
A paradox: divine transcendence named to make room for humble petition.
Hearing is the axis on which presence transfers from heaven to house.
Day and night attention: petition asks for uninterrupted divine regard.
The hearing that leads to pardon ties heaven‑dwelling and earthward prayer.
Legal oath and altar converge; human dispute brought under sacred hearing.
Divine justice heard from heaven right‑sized to human conduct; recompense and vindication.
Defeat framed as disciplinary context that can occasion return and confession.
Forgiveness is paired with restoration to ancestral land.
Drought as covenantal chastening; prayer toward the house becomes the channel for reversal.
Teaching (torah) and divine mercy together restore the land's fertility.
A catalogue of calamities: cosmic, biological, and military are included in the petition field.
Individual griefs join communal lifting of hands under one roof of plea.
Divine hearing attends to interior motives; recompense and mercy are heart‑sensitive.
The goal of hearing is formative: fear that leads to walking in the taught way.
The house becomes an access point for outsiders drawn by the fame and power of YHWH.
Foreign petitions answered make the name known and fear spread among nations.
War petitions are oriented toward the chosen city and house as locus of plea.
Divine adjudication sustains those who plead from the chosen center.
Acknowledges universal failing; captivity appears as consequence within covenant logic.
Captivity can become the scene of inward turning and confession.
Even from exile their hearts can orient toward the ancestral place and the house of name.
Hearing from heaven effects both judicial restoration and mercy for a penitent people.
A short, urgent plea for perpetual divine attentiveness upon the house.
Invocation for divine ascent: priests garmented in salvation, the faithful made joyful.
A final plea: do not withdraw from the anointed — recall David's mercies as covenant memory.

contemplative_note: Solomon's prayer locates divine presence beyond the house yet petitions YHWH to make the temple an axis for mercy, justice, and return.
safety_note: This chapter contains ancient ritual, warfare, and captivity language; treat ethically and do not use for modern violence justification.
